assessments.reasoning: Chapter 11 says the executable part stops and control proceeds to the matching handler, then to the next enclosing-block statement after normal handling. The local-handler scenario on physical PDF page 457 confirms that transfer without propagation.

challenge.method: Compare Figure 11-1, chapter 11’s textual overview and the declaration and exception-handler countercases.
challenge.results: A local matching handler prevents outward propagation if it finishes normally. The continuation is the next statement of the enclosing block. Handler, invoker, and host boundary cases differ.

limitations: The caller or host takes control when there is no enclosing block. Separate passages govern exceptions raised during a declaration or within a handler.
